page_title: Implementing High-Cardinality Instrumentation in Frontend Apps

summary.name: Honeycomb for Frontend Observability
summary.one_liner: A blog post by Honeycomb's product manager explaining how to add high-cardinality "wide event" instrumentation to frontend web apps using Honeycomb's OpenTelemetry-based Web SDK.
use_cases: Instrumenting a browser app to answer per-customer performance questions
Finding which page or script causes poor INP scores
Attaching user plan or team info to frontend traces
Tracking product funnel conditions such as login or cart adds
Comparing performance across browsers, devices, or releases
summary.what_it_does: The post contrasts aggregate metrics (such as P70 Core Web Vitals or average TTFB) with wide events that can answer detailed questions, such as which page had the worst INP and which customers are affected. It explains three ways to attach attributes to spans: session-level resource attributes set when the SDK is instantiated, dynamic attributes added via OpenTelemetry span processors as conditions are met, and span-specific attributes added through options like applyCustomAttributesOnSpan in instrumentation libraries. It states that Honeycomb's Web SDK collects wide events with little setup and that it supports up to 2000 attributes per span.
notable: Charges the same per event regardless of attribute count, and every attribute is queryable without pre-indexing
Built on OpenTelemetry, with span processors for attaching dynamic data during a session
caveats: Page does not give pricing; it only says to talk to the team for a custom demo or plan help
Describes Honeycomb's own SDK, so it is tied to that vendor's product
